keyVerseText: Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof, and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat,
rootMeaning: The root of גִּנְזַךְ (ginzak) is גֶּנֶז (genez), which conveys the idea of a chest or treasury, a place where valuable items are stored securely. Etymologically, גִּנְזַךְ is a prolonged form of גֶּנֶז, emphasizing an organized repository or treasury rather than just any container. This deepens the English gloss "treasury" by highlighting not only the stored wealth but also the intentional safeguarding and management of precious resources.
usageInScripture: The word גִּנְזַךְ appears only once in Scripture, specifically in 1 Chronicles 28:11, where it is translated as "treasuries." This singular occurrence shows a consistent usage referring to a secure place for storing valuable items, likely in the context of the temple or royal holdings. The limited usage underscores the word's specificity and importance in describing designated sacred or royal storage spaces.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גִּנְזַךְ as a treasury enriches our grasp of biblical themes related to stewardship and divine provision. Treasuries in Scripture often symbolize not merely material wealth but also the careful preservation of God's blessings and covenantal promises. For the Christian faith, this word reminds us of the responsibility to safeguard spiritual treasures entrusted to us, such as the gospel and the fruits of the Spirit. It also points to the order and intentionality God desires in His house and among His people, reflecting His holiness and sovereignty over all things.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 28:11, David gives Solomon the pattern of the porch, houses, treasuries, and inner chambers, highlighting the detailed planning for the temple. The use of גִּנְזַךְ here emphasizes the importance of the treasuries as distinct, secure places within the temple complex. This underscores the sacred care and provision for the house of God, reminding believers that God's presence is accompanied by the orderly management of what He entrusts to His people.
